ui.q1: What is the {a} price in {country} today?

about: {site} shows live prices for gold, silver, other metals, energy, crops, stocks, indices, cryptocurrencies and currencies in your own currency, for many countries and languages.
Prices come from public market data feeds and are updated every few minutes. Some prices are updated from public pages or by hand and show their source.
Local retail estimates add typical taxes, making charges and dealer premiums to the global price, with the sources and date shown. They are estimates, not quotes.
We also offer calculators for gold value, zakat, profit and units, a currency converter and price alerts.
privacy: We do not ask for accounts or personal data. We store only your language, country and theme choice in your browser.
Ads, when enabled, are served by Google AdSense, which may use cookies to show relevant ads. You can manage this in your Google ad settings.
Anonymous, aggregate visit statistics may be collected to improve the site.
contact: Questions, corrections or partnership requests: please use the contact address published on this page once the site is live.
If you see a wrong price, tell us the asset, the country and where you saw the correct value.
terms: By using {site} you agree to these terms. The site is provided for general information.
Prices, charts and estimates are indicative, may be delayed or wrong, and must not be used as the only basis for a trade or purchase.
You may not copy the data in bulk or resell it. For automated access use our free API and credit the site.
We may change or stop any part of the service at any time and we are not liable for losses from its use.
disclaimer: {site} is not a broker, bank or financial adviser and gives no investment advice.
Local retail estimates, bar premiums and buyback figures are estimates built from public sources. Shops differ, always confirm the price with the seller.
Past performance does not predict future results. Investing in metals, shares and cryptocurrencies carries risk, including the loss of the money invested.
cookies: We use only the browser storage needed to remember your language, country and theme.
Ads, when enabled, are served by Google AdSense, which may set cookies to show relevant ads. You can manage this in your Google ad settings.
Visitors in regions that require consent will be asked before advertising cookies are used.
developers: Our price API is free for small projects. Create a key below and send it in the x-api-key header.
Endpoints: /v1/overview for all prices and performance, /v1/chart/SYMBOL?days=365 for history, /v1/rates for currency rates.
Free keys allow 1,000 requests per day. Responses are cached for a minute, please do not call faster than that.
Please credit the site when you show our prices.

gold.about: Gold is the most widely held precious metal and a traditional store of value. Its price is quoted per troy ounce worldwide and per gram or tola in many local markets, with jewelry sold by karat from 10K to 24K.
drivers: Interest rates and the US dollar
Inflation and economic or political uncertainty
Central bank buying and investment demand

silver.about: Silver is both a precious metal and an industrial metal. It is priced per troy ounce and sold as bars, coins and jewelry in purities such as 999, 925 and 800.
drivers: Industrial demand from solar panels and electronics
The gold price and the US dollar
Investment demand for bars and coins

platinum.about: Platinum is a rare, dense precious metal that is more valuable by weight than gold in many periods. It is priced per troy ounce.
drivers: Mine supply, mostly from South Africa and Russia
Investment demand and the gold price

palladium.about: Palladium is a rare precious metal used mainly in petrol-car catalytic converters. It is priced per troy ounce.
drivers: Mine supply from Russia and South Africa

copper.about: Copper is the benchmark industrial metal. Its price is quoted per metric ton and is watched as a sign of global economic health.
drivers: Construction and manufacturing demand, especially in China
The US dollar and trade policy

aluminum.about: Aluminum is a light, widely used metal produced from bauxite with large amounts of electricity. Its price is quoted per metric ton.
drivers: Demand from cars, packaging and construction
Production in China and trade tariffs

nickel.about: Nickel is a metal used to make stainless steel and batteries. Its price is quoted per metric ton on the London Metal Exchange.
drivers: Supply from Indonesia and the Philippines

zinc.about: Zinc is mainly used to galvanize steel against rust. Its price is quoted per metric ton.
drivers: Energy prices in Europe and China

lead.about: Lead is a dense metal used mostly in vehicle batteries. Its price is quoted per metric ton.

tin.about: Tin is a rare metal used mostly as solder in electronics. Its price is quoted per metric ton.
drivers: Mine supply from Indonesia, Myanmar and Peru

cobalt.about: Cobalt is a battery metal mined mainly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its price is quoted per metric ton.
drivers: Congo mine supply and export rules

lithium.about: Lithium carbonate is the main raw material for rechargeable batteries. The price shown is for battery-grade carbonate in China, converted to US dollars per metric ton.

uranium.about: Uranium is the fuel of nuclear power plants. Its price is quoted in US dollars per pound of U3O8.
drivers: Nuclear plant restarts and new reactors
Mine output, mainly from Kazakhstan and Canada

iron-ore.about: Iron ore is the main raw material for steel. The price shown is for 62% iron content delivered to China, per metric ton.

steel.about: Steel is an alloy of iron used in almost every industry. The price shown is for steel rebar in China, converted to US dollars per metric ton.
drivers: Iron ore and coking coal costs

steel-hrc.about: Hot-rolled steel coil is a flat steel product used in manufacturing. The price shown is for US Midwest delivery per metric ton.
drivers: US demand from cars and construction

lumber.about: Lumber futures track the price of softwood used in building houses, quoted per 1,000 board feet.
drivers: Trade duties between the US and Canada

wti-oil.about: WTI is the US benchmark for crude oil, quoted per barrel and delivered in Cushing, Oklahoma.
drivers: Inventories, geopolitics and the US dollar

brent-oil.about: Brent is the global benchmark for crude oil, quoted per barrel, and prices most of the oil traded outside the US.
drivers: Global demand, especially from China and India
Conflicts and sanctions in producing regions

natural-gas.about: Natural gas is quoted here as the US Henry Hub price per MMBtu. It is used for heating, power generation and industry.

gasoline.about: Gasoline futures track wholesale petrol prices in US dollars per gallon.

heating-oil.about: Heating oil futures track wholesale diesel and heating fuel in US dollars per gallon.
drivers: Diesel demand from trucks and industry

wheat.about: Wheat is one of the world's main food grains. The price is quoted per bushel on the Chicago exchange.
drivers: Exports from Russia, Ukraine, the US and the EU
Stocks, energy prices and the US dollar

corn.about: Corn is a major food and feed grain and a source of ethanol. The price is quoted per bushel on the Chicago exchange.
drivers: Demand for ethanol and animal feed

soybeans.about: Soybeans are processed into oil and meal. The price is quoted per bushel on the Chicago exchange.

rice.about: Rough rice is a staple food for billions of people. The price is quoted per hundredweight on the Chicago exchange.
drivers: Monsoon and harvest conditions in Asia
Export rules of India, Thailand and Vietnam

sugar.about: Raw sugar futures track the world price of sugar, quoted in US dollars per pound.

coffee.about: Arabica coffee futures track the world price of coffee beans, quoted in US dollars per pound.

cocoa.about: Cocoa futures track the price of cocoa beans, quoted in US dollars per metric ton.
drivers: Harvests in Ivory Coast and Ghana

cotton.about: Cotton futures track the world price of raw cotton, quoted in US dollars per pound.
drivers: Weather in the US, India and China

bitcoin.about: Bitcoin is the first and largest cryptocurrency. It trades around the clock on exchanges and its supply is capped at 21 million coins.

ethereum.about: Ethereum is a blockchain for smart contracts and applications, and its coin, ether, is the second largest cryptocurrency.

bnb.about: BNB is the coin of the BNB Chain and the Binance exchange ecosystem.

xrp.about: XRP is a cryptocurrency used for fast international payments on the XRP Ledger.

solana.about: Solana is a fast blockchain for applications and payments, and SOL is its coin.

cardano.about: Cardano is a proof-of-stake blockchain, and ADA is its coin.

dogecoin.about: Dogecoin began as a joke coin and became one of the most traded cryptocurrencies.

tron.about: TRON is a blockchain widely used for stablecoin transfers, and TRX is its coin.

polkadot.about: Polkadot connects many blockchains, and DOT is its coin.

chainlink.about: Chainlink supplies real-world data to blockchains, and LINK is its coin.

litecoin.about: Litecoin is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created for faster payments than Bitcoin.

avalanche.about: Avalanche is a fast blockchain platform, and AVAX is its coin.

sp500.about: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest US companies and is the main gauge of the US stock market.

nasdaq.about: The Nasdaq Composite tracks thousands of shares listed on Nasdaq, with a strong weight in technology companies.

dow-jones.about: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 large US companies.

ftse-100.about: The FTSE 100 tracks the 100 largest companies listed in London.

dax.about: The DAX tracks 40 large German companies listed in Frankfurt.

cac-40.about: The CAC 40 tracks 40 large companies listed in Paris.

nikkei-225.about: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies listed in Tokyo.

hang-seng.about: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest companies listed in Hong Kong.

shanghai.about: The Shanghai Composite tracks all shares listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

nifty-50.about: The Nifty 50 tracks 50 large companies on India's National Stock Exchange.

sensex.about: The Sensex tracks 30 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

egx30.about: The EGX 30 tracks the 30 most active companies on the Egyptian Exchange.

tasi.about: The Tadawul All Share Index tracks all companies listed on the Saudi stock exchange.

bist-100.about: The BIST 100 tracks the 100 largest companies on Borsa Istanbul.

bovespa.about: The Bovespa tracks the main companies on Brazil's B3 exchange.

asx-200.about: The ASX 200 tracks the 200 largest companies on the Australian exchange.

tsx.about: The S&P/TSX Composite tracks the main companies on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

kospi.about: The KOSPI tracks all common shares on the Korea Exchange.

euro-stoxx-50.about: The Euro Stoxx 50 tracks 50 large companies of the euro area.
